# AGENTS.md - opencode-serper project memory

A small [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) V2 plugin that routes web search through
[Serper](https://serper.dev). It registers a `serper` websearch provider, a
`serper` `/connect` integration, and a namespace of `serper.*` search and
scraping tools. TypeScript, loaded directly by OpenCode's bun runtime - there is
no build step.

## Landing a change (jj, NOT git)

The owner uses **Jujutsu exclusively** in a colocated repo. **Never invoke
`git`** - it can corrupt jj's operation log. jj has no staging area; the working
copy is always a commit.

1. Make **one focused change** per commit.
2. Run `mise run check` (typecheck + tests); land only when it passes.
3. For user-visible changes, bump `version` in `package.json` + add a dated
   `CHANGELOG.md` entry in the *same* commit.
4. `jj describe -m "<imperative one-liner>"` then `jj bookmark set main --to @`
   then `jj new`.
5. Invariant: every time `main` moves, the next command is `jj new`, so `@` is
   always an empty commit one above main.

**Landing is strictly local. Agents must NEVER push from this repository.** Do
not run `jj git push`, create a PR as part of landing, or otherwise publish a
landed change. The owner handles all pushes.

Remote: `origin` = `Jarvvski/opencode-serper` (SSH:
`git@github.com:Jarvvski/opencode-serper.git`). `gh` auto-detection fails in jj
workspaces - always pass `-R Jarvvski/opencode-serper`.

## Toolchain

**mise** owns the runtime and the tasks (`mise.toml`). Use the tasks, don't
hand-roll commands:

- `mise run check` - the pre-land gate: typecheck + tests.
- `mise run typecheck` / `mise run test` - individual steps.

Bun, TypeScript, `bun.lock` committed. No build step: `package.json` `exports`
ships `./src/index.ts`, which OpenCode loads with its own bun runtime. Keep
`src/serper.ts` (transport + pure mappers) free of plugin-API coupling so it
stays unit-testable.

## Versioning & changelog

Keep a single **version of record**: `version` in `package.json`. Semver: PATCH
for fixes, MINOR otherwise; **never bump to 1.0.0 (or any MAJOR) without the
owner's explicit approval - do not auto-bump.** A user-visible change adds a
dated `CHANGELOG.md` entry (newest first) in the same commit; skip pure internal
refactors.

## Plugin API notes (OpenCode 2.0.27)

- Target `@opencode/plugin` `^2.0.27`, the V2 SDK. The V1 `@opencode-ai/plugin`
  package is unrelated.
- A plugin is `Plugin.define({ id, setup })`; `setup(ctx)` registers
  `ctx.integration`, `ctx.websearch`, and `ctx.tool` transforms.
- `IntegrationEditor` has no `add`; `update(id, ...)` **upserts**, which is how
  the `serper` integration is registered.
- Websearch results are `{ url, title?, content?, time: { published? } }`; `url`
  and `time` are required. `execute(input, { signal })` receives an
  `AbortSignal` - pass it to `fetch`.
- **Install specs.** `opencode plugin add` accepts npm names (with versions,
  tags, ranges) and npm-compatible Git specs (`github:Jarvvski/opencode-serper`,
  what this repo uses) but rejects local paths. The `plugins` config array does
  accept local paths (`./plugins/local`, `/absolute/path/plugin.ts`), and a
  `.ts`/`.js` file dropped in `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` is loaded directly.
- **Runtime SDK comes from our own `dependencies`.** OpenCode installs the
  plugin with npm and fetches `@opencode/plugin` from our `package.json`; the
  server does not provide it. So the pinned version in `package.json` (currently
  exact `2.0.27`) is what runs, and CI typechecks against it - keep them aligned
  when bumping.
- Plugin changes need a server restart to load; `opencode reload` does not
  reconcile plugins.

## Secrets

Never log or echo the API key. Resolve it only in `src/key.ts`, and keep
`opencode.jsonc` examples free of secrets - use `/connect`, `SERPER_API_KEY`, or
`options.apiKey`.

# Opencode-Serper

[![CI](https://github.com/Jarvvski/opencode-serper/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Jarvvski/opencode-serper/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE)

Serper web search and scraping for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai). Registers
[Serper](https://serper.dev) as a `websearch` provider — so the built-in search
tool, and every agent that already uses it, search through Serper — and adds a
namespace of `serper.*` tools for the rest of Serper's endpoints.

**Status:** `0.1.0`, pre-1.0. Installed from Git; not yet published to npm.

## Quickstart

```sh
opencode plugin add github:Jarvvski/opencode-serper
```

Restart OpenCode, then run `/connect`, choose **Serper**, and paste your API key.
Serper is now the default web search provider: ask for current information and
the built-in `websearch` tool uses it.

That is the whole setup. Agents can additionally call the `serper.*` tools
(`news`, `scholar`, `places`, `images`, `autocomplete`, `scrape`) in Code Mode.

Installing the plugin makes Serper the default search provider. To keep another
provider and use only the `serper.*` tools, pass `options: { "setDefault": false }`
— see [configuration](docs/configuration.md#web-search-provider).

Full walkthrough, every tool, and troubleshooting:
**[docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md)**.

- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md) — key resolution, options, env, permissions.
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) — how the plugin registers and maps results.
- [ADRs](docs/adr/) — design decisions.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) — what has landed.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here (newest first). The
version of record lives in `package.json`.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-12

### Added

- Initial release. Registers Serper as an OpenCode `websearch` provider, adds a
  `serper` integration connectable with `/connect` (key) or `SERPER_API_KEY`
  (env), and exposes `serper.*` search and scraping tools (`search`, `news`,
  `scholar`, `places`, `images`, `autocomplete`, `scrape`).
- `options.setDefault: false` to keep another `websearch` provider as the default
  instead of selecting Serper on install.

### Changed

- `serper.*` tool results are capped at 20,000 characters (`MAX_TOOL_CONTENT`) so
  a large scrape or image response cannot exhaust the model's context window.
- Key resolution falls through to the plugin option or `SERPER_API_KEY` when the
  credential store cannot be read, instead of failing the whole request.

# opencode-serper

An OpenCode plugin that routes web search through [Serper](https://serper.dev)
and exposes Serper's search and scraping endpoints as agent tools.

## Language

### Core

**Provider**:
The Serper-backed implementation of OpenCode's `websearch` provider interface.
Selecting it makes the built-in `websearch` tool search via Serper.
_Avoid_: search backend, engine

**Integration**:
The OpenCode credential record named `serper`, connected with `/connect` or from
`SERPER_API_KEY`. It stores the API key outside `opencode.jsonc`.
_Avoid_: account, auth

**Credential**:
The stored API key behind an integration connection.
_Avoid_: token, secret

**Tool namespace**:
The `serper` group under which the plugin's tools appear in Code Mode
(`tools.serper.search`, `tools.serper.scrape`, ...).
_Avoid_: toolset, toolkit

**API key resolution**:
The ordered lookup for the Serper key - integration credential, then the
`apiKey` plugin option, then `SERPER_API_KEY`.
_Avoid_: key lookup

# Security Policy

## Supported versions

This project is pre-1.0 and ships from `main`; only the latest commit is
supported. Pin a specific commit if you need stability.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please do **not** open a public issue for a security problem.

Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on this repository
(**Security → Report a vulnerability**), or email the maintainer at the address
on the [GitHub profile](https://github.com/Jarvvski).

Include what you can: affected version or commit, a description, reproduction
steps, and impact. You will get an acknowledgement as soon as possible.

## Handling of secrets

This plugin never logs or echoes your Serper API key. The key is resolved in
`src/key.ts` only, and configuration examples in `docs/` contain no secrets.
Prefer `/connect` (OpenCode's credential store) over putting a key in
`opencode.jsonc`. If you believe a key has leaked, rotate it in the Serper
dashboard.

# Architecture

`opencode-serper` is a single OpenCode V2 plugin. On load it registers three
things through the plugin context, then gets out of the way.

```
src/index.ts      Plugin.define({ id: "serper", setup })
  ├─ ctx.integration  → registers the "serper" integration (key + env methods)
  ├─ src/provider.ts  → registers the "serper" websearch provider
  └─ src/tools.ts     → registers the serper.* tools
src/key.ts        key resolution (integration → option → env)
src/serper.ts     HTTP transport + pure result mappers (no plugin coupling)
```

## Registration

`setup(ctx)` runs three transforms:

1. **Integration** (`ctx.integration.transform`) - upserts a `serper` integration
   with a `key` method (for `/connect`) and an `env` method named
   `SERPER_API_KEY`. `IntegrationEditor` has no `add`; `update` upserts.
2. **Websearch provider** (`ctx.websearch.transform`) - adds a provider with id
   `serper` and selects it as the default. Its `execute({ query }, { signal })`
   calls `google.serper.dev/search` and maps the organic results into OpenCode's
   result shape.
3. **Tools** (`ctx.tool.transform`) - namespaces `serper` and adds one tool per
   endpoint the websearch provider interface does not cover.

Each transform returns a registration the plugin does not need to dispose: the
plugin is loaded once per server and lives for its lifetime.

## Why a plugin

OpenCode's built-in `websearch` tool ships five providers (Exa, Firecrawl,
Parallel, Tavily, TinyFish); Serper is not one. A plugin can register a websearch
provider, so the built-in tool - and every agent that already uses it - can
search via Serper without per-agent wiring. See
[adr/0001-ship-as-an-opencode-plugin.md](adr/0001-ship-as-an-opencode-plugin.md).

## Result mapping

OpenCode's websearch result is:

```ts
interface WebSearchResult {
  url: string            // required
  title?: string
  content?: string
  time: { published?: number }  // required, may be empty
}
```

`src/serper.ts` maps a Serper organic row (`{ title, link, snippet, date }`)
into it: `link` → `url`, `snippet` → `content`, and a parseable `date` →
`time.published`. Rows without a `link` are dropped. The mapper is pure, so it is
covered by unit tests without touching the network.

The `serper.*` tools do not use this shape - they return the raw Serper JSON as a
text result, since each endpoint (news, places, images, ...) has its own fields.
That JSON is capped at `MAX_TOOL_CONTENT` (20,000 characters) by `truncate`, so a
large scrape cannot blow the model's context window; the cut is marked with the
original size.

Because the provider only maps `snippet` into `content`, the built-in `websearch`
tool answers from search snippets rather than full page content. That is the
trade-off for routing the built-in tool through Serper; the `scrape` tool is the
escape hatch for full page text.

## Key resolution

`src/key.ts` resolves the key in order: the active `serper` integration
credential, then the `apiKey` plugin option, then `SERPER_API_KEY`. It is the
only module that reads the key, so a key never reaches logs or error messages.
See [adr/0002-connect-credential-over-config.md](adr/0002-connect-credential-over-config.md).

## Error handling

`src/serper.ts` throws on a non-2xx response with the status and a truncated
body. A missing key throws an actionable error naming all three sources. Both
surface through the tool result; nothing is swallowed.

# Configuration

`opencode-serper` needs one thing: a Serper API key. Everything else has a
sensible default.

## API key resolution

The plugin resolves the key in this order, first match wins:

1. **Integration credential** - the `serper` connection created by `/connect`
   (or sourced from the `SERPER_API_KEY` env method the plugin registers).
2. **Plugin option** - `options.apiKey` in the `plugins` entry.
3. **Environment variable** - `SERPER_API_KEY` in OpenCode's environment.

If none is set, any Serper call fails with an actionable error naming all three.

### Via `/connect` (recommended)

Run `/connect` in the TUI, choose **Serper**, and paste your key. The key is
stored in OpenCode's credential store, outside `opencode.jsonc`. This keeps it
out of dotfiles and matches how OpenCode's own providers handle credentials.

The same flow is available from the CLI:

```sh
opencode auth login serper
```

### Via the environment

```sh
export SERPER_API_KEY=your-key
opencode
```

The plugin registers an `env` method for the `serper` integration, so a set
`SERPER_API_KEY` also satisfies `/connect`.

> **Caveat.** The key is read from the environment of the OpenCode **background
> service**, not the shell you launch the TUI from. If a service is already
> running, exporting `SERPER_API_KEY` in a new shell has no effect until you
> restart it (`opencode service restart`). `/connect` stores the key in the
> credential store and avoids this entirely.

### Via a plugin option

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "github:Jarvvski/opencode-serper",
      "options": { "apiKey": "your-key" },
    },
  ],
}
```

This puts the secret in `opencode.jsonc`, so prefer `/connect` or the
environment unless the config is not tracked or you are running in CI.

## Web search provider

Installing the plugin selects `serper` as the default `websearch` provider, so
the built-in `websearch` tool searches via Serper with no further setup. To set
it explicitly, or to switch back to another provider:

```jsonc
{
  "websearch": { "provider": "serper" },
}
```

To keep your own provider choice and only use the `serper.*` tools, opt out of
the default with `options.setDefault: false`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    { "package": "github:Jarvvski/opencode-serper", "options": { "setDefault": false } },
  ],
}
```

Serper's `websearch` provider maps the organic `snippet` into the result
`content`, so answers are built from search snippets rather than full page
content. If you want fuller content from the built-in tool, keep another
provider as the default and use the `serper.*` tools for Serper's endpoints.

See OpenCode's [websearch docs](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/websearch) for the
provider list and selection behaviour.

## Permissions

The built-in `websearch` tool uses OpenCode's `websearch` permission action with
the query as the resource; the `serper.*` tools use `serper_*` actions. The
default policy allows both. To require approval before searches:

```jsonc
{
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "websearch", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
  ],
}
```

See OpenCode's [permissions docs](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/permissions).

# Usage

How to install, connect, and use `opencode-serper`. For a quick start see the
[README](../README.md); this page is the fuller reference.

## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add github:Jarvvski/opencode-serper
```

This adds the Git spec to the `plugins` array in your global `opencode.jsonc`.
Restart OpenCode so the plugin loads.

The package is not published to npm yet, so install from the Git spec above
rather than the package name. Once it is on npm, `opencode plugin add
@jarvvski/opencode-serper` will work the same way.

## Connect the API key

Pick one:

1. **`/connect` (recommended).** Run `/connect` in the TUI, choose **Serper**,
   and paste your key. It is stored in OpenCode's credential store, outside
   `opencode.jsonc`.
2. **Environment variable.** Export `SERPER_API_KEY` before starting OpenCode.
   The key is read by the background service, so if one is already running,
   restart it (`opencode service restart`) after changing the variable.
3. **Plugin option.** Pass the key explicitly in `opencode.jsonc`:

   ```jsonc
   {
     "plugins": [
       { "package": "github:Jarvvski/opencode-serper", "options": { "apiKey": "..." } },
     ],
   }
   ```

The plugin resolves the key in this order: `/connect` credential, then
`options.apiKey`, then `SERPER_API_KEY`. See
[configuration.md](configuration.md#api-key-resolution) for details.

## Search

Installing the plugin registers Serper as a `websearch` provider and selects it
as the default, so the built-in `websearch` tool - and any agent that uses it -
searches through Serper with no further setup.

To be explicit, or to switch back to another provider:

```jsonc
{
  "websearch": { "provider": "serper" },
}
```

To keep another provider as the default and use only the `serper.*` tools, pass
`options.setDefault: false` when configuring the plugin. See
[configuration.md](configuration.md#web-search-provider).

Then ask for current information:

```text
Find the latest Jujutsu release and summarize what changed.
```

## Tools

The `websearch` provider only covers web search, so the plugin also exposes
Serper's other endpoints as tools. Agents reach them in Code Mode as
`tools.serper.<name>`; each returns the Serper response as pretty-printed JSON.

| Tool           | Endpoint                 | Input                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| `search`       | `google.serper.dev/search` | `q`, `gl?`, `hl?`, `num?`  |
| `news`         | `google.serper.dev/news`   | `q`, `gl?`, `hl?`, `num?`  |
| `scholar`      | `google.serper.dev/scholar`| `q`, `num?`                |
| `places`       | `google.serper.dev/places` | `q`, `gl?`, `hl?`          |
| `images`       | `google.serper.dev/images` | `q`, `gl?`, `hl?`, `num?`  |
| `autocomplete` | `google.serper.dev/autocomplete` | `q`, `gl?`, `hl?`   |
| `scrape`       | `scrape.serper.dev`        | `url`                      |

- `q` - the search query.
- `gl` - Google country code, e.g. `us`, `gb`.
- `hl` - Google language code, e.g. `en`.
- `num` - number of results, `1`-`100`.
- `url` - absolute URL to scrape.

### Examples

Ask an agent in plain language and it will pick the tool:

```text
Search the news for "open source AI coding agent" from the last week.
```

```text
Scrape https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/websearch and summarize the providers it lists.
```

Or call the tools directly in Code Mode:

```js
const results = await tools.serper.search({ q: "jujutsu vcs", gl: "us", hl: "en", num: 5 })
const article = await tools.serper.scrape({ url: "https://jj-vcs.dev/latest/changelog/" })
```

## Troubleshooting

**Search fails with "Serper is not configured".** The plugin could not resolve a
key. Run `/connect` and choose Serper, or set `SERPER_API_KEY`, or pass
`options.apiKey`. See [configuration.md](configuration.md#api-key-resolution).

**The plugin does not load.** Plugin changes need a server restart; `opencode
reload` does not reconcile plugins. After adding a local plugin, restart the
service (`opencode service restart`).

**HTTP 401 / 403 from Serper.** The stored key is wrong or revoked. Reconnect
with `/connect`, or replace `SERPER_API_KEY`.

**HTTP 429.** Serper rate limit. Wait and retry, or check your Serper plan.

# Ship as an OpenCode plugin, not a wrapper or an MCP server

OpenCode's built-in `websearch` tool ships five providers - Exa, Firecrawl,
Parallel, Tavily, and TinyFish - and Serper is not one. We wanted the built-in
`websearch` tool, and every agent that already uses it, to search via Serper
without teaching each agent a separate tool.

An OpenCode V2 plugin can register a websearch provider
(`ctx.websearch.transform`), so we ship one: a `serper` provider, plus a
namespace of `serper.*` tools for the endpoints the provider interface does not
cover (news, scholar, places, images, autocomplete, scrape). The provider makes
search work everywhere the built-in tool is used; the tools cover the rest.

The alternatives were a standalone MCP server - the route we started with, and
what the Serper ecosystem offers - or a thin wrapper. Both leave `websearch`
pointed at another provider and require per-agent wiring to prefer Serper, so the
built-in search path never routes through it.

Status: accepted

# Store the Serper key in the OpenCode credential store, not the config

The plugin needs a Serper API key. The obvious place is a `plugins[].options`
value in `opencode.jsonc`, but that config is a candidate for the owner's
chezmoi-tracked dotfiles, and OpenCode's own search providers do not store
credentials in config at all.

We chose the `/connect` integration. The plugin registers a `serper` integration
with a `key` method (paste the key in the TUI) and an `env` method named
`SERPER_API_KEY`, and resolves the key from the active connection first. The key
lives in OpenCode's credential store, outside any tracked file, and the flow
matches how OpenCode's built-in providers handle credentials.

Two fallbacks remain, for CI and non-interactive use where `/connect` is not
available: the `apiKey` plugin option, then the raw `SERPER_API_KEY` environment
variable. Resolution order is credential, then option, then env.

The trade-off: the credential store is per-OpenCode-install, so a second machine
needs its own `/connect` (or the env var). That is the same behaviour as every
other OpenCode integration.

Status: accepted
